records.question: How is Job’s character described?
records.answer: He was blameless and righteous and honored God and turned from evil.

records.question: After Job’s sons held feasts with their brothers and sisters in their houses, what would Job do?
records.answer: Job would consecrate them to God, offer burnt offerings, and pray for them.

records.question: Why did Yahweh say Satan should consider Job?
records.answer: There was no one like Job on the earth, a blameless and upright man, one who feared God and turned away from evil.

records.question: How did Satan say Yahweh had protected Job?
records.answer: He made a hedge around Job, around his house, and around all that he had on every side.

records.question: What did Satan think would cause Job to renounce God?
records.answer: He said to Job would renounce God if God attacked all Job’s possessions.

records.question: What did Yahweh give Satan permission to do?
records.answer: He gave Satan permission to take everything from Job, but not to lay a hand on his person.

records.question: What did the messenger tell Job the Sabeans had done to him?
records.answer: They killed all Job’s servants in the field and took away all the oxen and donkeys.

records.question: What did the second messenger tell Job had happened to his sheep?
records.answer: The fire of God fell from the heavens and burned them up along with the servants.

records.question: What did the third messenger tell Job had happened to his camels?
records.answer: Three groups of robbers came and attacked them. They stole all the camels and killed all the men that were caring for them.

records.question: What news did the fourth messenger bring to Job?
records.answer: Job’s sons and daughters were feasting in their brother’s home when a great wind came and struck the house, which collapsed on them and killed them.

records.question: What did Job do after he got all these messages?
records.answer: Job tore his robe, shaved his head, lay facedown on the ground, and worshiped God.

records.question: What did Job say about his condition after these events?
records.answer: He said he came naked from his mother’s womb, and he would return naked.

records.question: What did Job say that Yahweh had done to him?
records.answer: Yahweh gave, and Yahweh has taken away.

records.question: How did Job show that he was not a foolish man?
records.answer: Job did not sin, nor did he foolishly accuse God.

records.question: Who came with the sons of God when they presented themselves before Yahweh?
records.answer: Satan also came and presented himself.

records.question: What did Satan tell Yahweh that he had been doing?
records.answer: He said he was going to and fro on the earth, and walking back and forth on it.

records.question: How did Yahweh say that Job continued to do after Satan’s attacks?
records.answer: Job held fast to his integrity.

records.question: What does Satan want to do to Job now so that Job will curse God?
records.answer: Satan wants to touch Job’s bones and his body to hurt him.

records.question: How did Satan afflict Job’s body?
records.answer: He afflicted Job with severe boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

records.question: What did Job do to deal with the pain of his affliction?
records.answer: He took a potshard and scraped himself as he sat in ashes.

records.question: What did Job’s wife want him to do?
records.answer: Job’s wife wanted him to curse God and die.

records.question: What accusation did Job make to his wife?
records.answer: He accused her of thinking they should receive good at the hand of God but not evil.

records.question: What did Job’s three friends do when they heard what happened to Job?
records.answer: They came to mourn with him and comfort him.

records.question: How did the three friends of Job show their grief when they saw him?
records.answer: They raised their voices and wept, tore their robes, threw dust on their heads, and sat on the ground in silence for seven days and nights.

records.question: What did Job say about the day he was born?
records.answer: He cursed the day he was born and asked that it would perish.

records.question: What does Job want to claim the day he was born?
records.answer: He wants that day to be claimed by darkness and the shadow of death.

records.question: What does Job want to seize the night he was conceived?
records.answer: Job wants that night to be seized by gloom.

records.question: What did Job wish had happened when he came out of the womb?
records.answer: He wishes he had died at birth.

records.question: What does Job say he would be doing now if he had died at birth?
records.answer: He would be sleeping and at rest with kings and counselors of the earth.

records.question: From what are prisoners and servants released in death?
records.answer: The prisoner is released from the voice of the slave driver, and the servant is free from his master.

records.question: To whom does Job say that death will not come?
records.answer: It does not come to the one who longs for death and who searches for it more than those who search for hidden treasure.

records.question: How does Job describe his groaning?
records.answer: His groaning flows out like water.

records.question: What are the things that troubles have replaced in Job’s life?
records.answer: He cannot be at ease or quiet and has no rest.

records.question: What good things does Eliphaz say Job has done for others?
records.answer: Job had instructed many and strengthened weak hands.

records.question: What does Eliphaz say is Job’s confidence and hope in time of trouble?
records.answer: Job’s fear of God is his confidence, and the integrity of his ways is his hope.

records.question: Who perishes by the breath of God and his anger?
records.answer: Those who plow misery and sow trouble perish and cease to exist.

records.question: What does Eliphaz says is broken?
records.answer: The teeth of young lions are broken.

records.question: How did Eliphaz secretly receive a certain message?
records.answer: He heard a whisper in his ear and saw visions in the night.

records.question: What came upon Eliphaz when he received the message?
records.answer: Fear and trembling came on him.

records.question: What did the voice ask about mortal men?
records.answer: It asked if a mortal man can be more righteous than God, more pure than his Maker.

records.question: How does Eliphaz describe mortal men?
records.answer: They live in houses of clay with their foundation in the dust, and they are crushed sooner than a moth.

records.question: What does Eliphaz say will happen to a foolish and simple man?
records.answer: Indignation kills the foolish man, and resentment kills the simple one.

records.question: What happens to the children of the foolish person in the city gate?
records.answer: They are unsafe, they are crushed in the gate and are not rescued.

records.question: From where does trouble really come?
records.answer: All his life, man makes his own trouble.

records.question: What does God give to the earth and the fields?
records.answer: He gives rain on the earth and sends water on the fields.

records.question: What does God do the schemes of crafty people?
records.answer: He frustrates their schemes so that their hands cannot carry out their plots.

records.question: From what does God save the needy and poor person?
records.answer: He saves the poor person from the threats and accusations of the mighty and saves the needy person from harm by the mighty people.

records.question: Why is the man happy whom God corrects and chastens?
records.answer: He is happy because the wounds, God binds up wounds, and his hands heal.

records.question: At what will the man whom God corrects laugh?
records.answer: He will laugh at destruction and famine.

records.question: What will the man whom God corrects find when he visits his sheepfold?
records.answer: He will find that nothing will be missing.

records.question: How long will the man whom God corrects live?
records.answer: He will come to his grave at a full age.

records.question: How does Job describe his anguish and his calamity?
records.answer: If his anguish and calamity were weighed, they would be heavier than the sand of the seas.

records.question: What has the Almighty done to Job with his arrows?
records.answer: His arrows are in Job, and Job’s spirit drinks up the poison.

records.question: What food does Job say has no taste?
records.answer: He says the white of an egg does not have any taste.

records.question: What one request does Job long for God to grant him?
records.answer: He wants God to crush him and cut him loose from his life.

records.question: What is Job’s consolation?
records.answer: His consolation is that he has not have denied the words of the Holy One.

records.question: What has been taken away from Job?
records.answer: Initiative has been taken away from him.

records.question: To whom should a friend show faithfulness?
records.answer: A friend should show faithfulness to the despairing person.

records.question: How does Job compare his brothers to a desert streambed?
records.answer: They have dealt treacherously like a wadi: they disappear in the dry season.

records.question: What happened to the caravans when they looked for water in these streams?
records.answer: They wandered into barren land and then perished. They were disappointed and deceived.

records.question: Why were Job’s friends nothing to him?
records.answer: They saw his dreadful situation and were afraid, so they did not help him.

records.question: What does Job say he will do if his friends would teach him?
records.answer: He will be silent.

records.question: What does Job say his friends plan to do with his words?
records.answer: They plan to correct his words and ignore what he has said.

records.question: Why does Job say his friends should relent in their attacks on him?
records.answer: Job’s cause is just.

records.question: To what does Job compare his months of misery and trouble-filled nights?
records.answer: He compares them to a slave desiring relief from heat, or a hired man looking for his wages.

records.question: What covers Job’s flesh?
records.answer: Worms and clods of dust, open sores and infection cover his flesh.

records.question: What image does Job use to describe the speed of his days?
records.answer: His days pass more swiftly than a weaver’s shuttle.

records.question: To what does Job compare the man who goes down to Sheol?
records.answer: He is like a cloud that is consumed and vanishes away.

records.question: In what way will Job speak and complain?
records.answer: He will speak in the anguish of his spirit and complain in the bitterness of his soul.

records.question: What does God do to Job when Job goes to bed?
records.answer: God scares him with dreams and terrifies him through visions.

records.question: Why did Job want God to leave him alone?
records.answer: Job said his days are useless.

records.question: What does Job ask God to let him alone long enough to do?
records.answer: He asks to be left alone long enough to swallow his own saliva.

records.question: What does Job think God will not do?
records.answer: Job thinks God will not pardon his transgression and take away his iniquity.

records.question: To what did Bildad compare the words of Job’s mouth?
records.answer: He compared them to a mighty wind.

records.question: How did Bildad say he knew that Job’s children sinned?
records.answer: He said he knew this because God had punished them for their sins.

records.question: How does Bildad say that God would bless Job if Job were pure and upright?
records.answer: God would reward Job by restoring his former home and wealth.

records.question: To what does Bildad compare our days on earth?
records.answer: He says they are a shadow.

records.question: What do papyrus and reeds require in order to grow?
records.answer: Papyrus requires a marsh, and reeds need water to grow.

records.question: To what does Bildad compare the trust of godless men?
records.answer: Their trust is as fragile as a spider’s web.

records.question: What do the roots do that represent a person that forgets God?
records.answer: The roots are wrapped around heaps of stone and look for good places among the rocks.

records.question: How does God treat the innocent man and the evildoers differently?
records.answer: He will not cast away an innocent man, but will not take the hand of evildoers.

records.question: With what will God fill the mouth and lips of the innocent man?
records.answer: He will fill his mouth with laughter and his lips with shouting.

records.question: What would happen is a man tried to argue with God?
records.answer: The man could not answer God once in a thousand times.

records.question: What does God do to the mountains when he is angry?
records.answer: He removes the mountains without warning and overturns them.

records.question: What does God trample down?
records.answer: He tramples down and subdues the waves of the sea.

records.question: Does Job see God when he passes by?
records.answer: God goes by him and Job does not see or perceive him.

records.question: Even if Job were righteous, how would he need to address God?
records.answer: Job could not answer him, but could only plead for mercy.

records.question: Why does Job believe God has multiple his wounds?
records.answer: Job believed God multiplied his wounds without cause.

records.question: Is it possible for Job to be righteous and perfect?
records.answer: No, even then, his mouth would condemn him and prove him guilty.

records.question: Does Job think God treats righteous and wicked people differently?
records.answer: He says God destroys both perfect people and wicked people together.

records.question: To what three things does Job compare the speed of his days?
records.answer: They are swifter than a running messenger, they are as fast as reed boats, and as fast as the swooping eagle.

records.question: Why did Job say it would be in vain to forget about his complaints?
records.answer: God would not consider him innocent, but Job would be condemned.

records.question: What does Job say that no judge would be able to do?
records.answer: No judge would lay his hand on both Job and God.

records.question: What does Job say no other judge could do?
records.answer: There is no other judge who can take God’s rod from Job, or keep God’s terror from frightening Job.

records.question: Why does Job want God to show him instead of merely condemning him?
records.answer: He wants God to show Job why he accuses him.

records.question: What kind of eyes does Job ask God if he has?
records.answer: Job asks him if he has eyes of flesh and sees like a man sees.

records.question: For what does Job say that God seeks and searches?
records.answer: God inquires after Job’s iniquity and searches after his sin.

records.question: What had God’s hands done for Job?
records.answer: They had framed and fashioned Job, yet they are destroying him.

records.question: With what did God clothe Job?
records.answer: He clothed him with skin and flesh.

records.question: What has God granted to Job?
records.answer: God granted him life and covenant faithfulness.

records.question: What would God do if Job sinned?
records.answer: God will notice his sin, and not acquit him of his iniquity.

records.question: What would God do to Job if Job’s head were lifted up?
records.answer: God would hunt him down like a lion.

records.question: Who would God bring against Job?
records.answer: God would bring new witnesses against him.

records.question: What does Job wish had happened to him?
records.answer: He wishes he had died and that no eye had ever seen him.

records.question: Where is Job going, from which he will not return?
records.answer: He is going to the land of darkness.

records.question: What did Zophar think Job had done to their teaching?
records.answer: He thought Job had mocked his friends’ teaching.

records.question: What does Zophar say that God has demanded from Job?
records.answer: He said God has demanded less from Job than his iniquity deserved.

records.question: Does Zophar think that Job could possibly understand God?
records.answer: Zophar thinks that it is impossible because God is as high as the heavens, deeper than Sheol, longer than the earth, and wider than the sea.

records.question: Does Zophar think that it is possible for anyone to stop God?
records.answer: It is impossible to stop God because he knows false people and punishes iniquity.

records.question: When does Zophar say foolish people will have understanding?
records.answer: They will have understanding when the colt of a wild donkey will be born to a man, meaning never!

records.question: What does Zophar say would happen to Job’s misery if he truly puts away his iniquity?
records.answer: Job would forget his misery and remember it only like waters that have flowed away.

records.question: Why would Job be secure if he put away his iniquity?
records.answer: He would be secure because there would be hope.

records.question: What does Zophar say will be the hope of wicked people?
records.answer: He says that their hope will be an expiration of breath, meaning that they can only hope to die.

records.question: How does Job compare himself to his friends?
records.answer: He says he also has understanding and is not inferior to them.

records.question: What do Job’s neighbors think of him now?
records.answer: They laugh at him.

records.question: Who does Job think could teach his friends?
records.answer: The beasts, the birds, the earth, and the fish of the sea could teach his friends.

records.question: What do all of the animals know?
records.answer: They know that the hand of Yahweh has given them life.

records.question: What does Job say about aged men and understanding?
records.answer: Wisdom and understanding come as people grow old.

records.question: What does God do with the waters?
records.answer: He with holds them and they dry up, and he sends them out and they overwhelm the land.

records.question: What does God take from kings?
records.answer: He takes off the chain of authority from them.

records.question: What does Job say about what God does to the trustworthy and the elders?
records.answer: He can remove the speech of the trustworthy and take away the understanding of elders.

records.question: What does Job say about God does to nations?
records.answer: He makes them strong or destroys them, and enlarges them or leads them along as prisoners.

records.question: What happens to the leaders of the people of the earth when God takes away their understanding?
records.answer: He causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no path.

records.question: How does Job say his knowledge compares to that of his friends?
records.answer: Job says that he knows the same as they know, and he is not inferior to them.

records.question: Who would Job like to talk to instead of his friends and why?
records.answer: He would rather speak to the Almighty because Job wants to reason with God.

records.question: What does Job say about wanting his friends to be silent?
records.answer: He says that the silence of his friends would be wisdom.

records.question: What does Job want his friends to hear?
records.answer: He wants them to listen to his reasoning and the pleading of his lips.

records.question: Would God approve if Job’s friends were showing favoritism?
records.answer: No, he would strongly reprove them if they showed favoritism.

records.question: What does Job think about his friends’ sayings and defenses?
records.answer: He says their sayings are proverbs made of ashes, and their defenses are made of clay.

records.question: What does Job ask his friends to do so that he may speak?
records.answer: Job asks them to hold their peace and let him speak.

records.question: Why does Job think that he would be acquitted?
records.answer: He does not come before God like a godless man.

records.question: What has Job set in order?
records.answer: He has set his defense in order.

records.question: What does Job want God to withdraw from him?
records.answer: Job wants God to withdraw his oppressive hand from Job and stop terrifying him.

records.question: Who does God treat Job like?
records.answer: He treats Job like his enemy.

records.question: What useless things does Job say he is like?
records.answer: He is like a rotten thing that wastes away, like a garment that moths have eaten.

records.question: How does Job say man is like a flower?
records.answer: Man sprouts from the ground like a flower, and then withers.

records.question: Who decides the lifespan of man?
records.answer: God has determined his days and the number of his months.

records.question: What does Job say about a tree that has been cut down?
records.answer: There can be hope for a tree that has been cut down, for it can sprout again.

records.question: Does Job say a man can live again?
records.answer: He says that people do not rise up again, and will not be roused out of their sleep.

records.question: Where does Job wish would God would hide him?
records.answer: Job wants God to hide him away in Sheol, away from troubles.

records.question: How would God treat Job’s transgression and iniquity if God’s wrath were finished?
records.answer: God would seal up Job’s transgression in a bag, and cover up Job’s iniquity.

records.question: What amazing thing can water do over time?
records.answer: Water can wear down stones.

records.question: What kinds of things does a dead man not know about his sons (his children)?
records.answer: If they achieve honor or become insignificant, he does not know it.

records.question: With what should a wise man not fill himself?
records.answer: He should not fill himself with the east wind.

records.question: How does Eliphaz think that Job’s statements dishonored God?
records.answer: He thinks Job destroys fear and diminishes devotion to God.

records.question: Does Eliphaz think that Job knows something that the other friends do not know?
records.answer: He does not think that Job knows what they do not know, or that he understands they do not understand.

records.question: Which people does Eliphaz say agree with Job’s friends?
records.answer: The gray-headed and very aged men who are older than Job’s father are with Eliphaz and his friends.

records.question: What does Eliphaz think Job has done?
records.answer: He thinks Job has turned his spirit against God.

records.question: How does God view his holy ones and the heavens?
records.answer: He puts no trust even in his holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in his sight.

records.question: From whom did Eliphaz get the things he will announce to Job?
records.answer: The things he has seen are things that wise men passed down from their fathers, and things that ancestors did not hide.

records.question: When will the destroyer come upon the wicked man?
records.answer: The destroyer will come upon him while he is in his prosperity.

records.question: What waits for the wicked man?
records.answer: The sword waits for the wicked man.

records.question: With what does the wicked man run against God?
records.answer: He runs at God with a stiff neck and a thick shield.

records.question: What will happen to the cities and houses of the wicked man?
records.answer: They are ready to become heaps.

records.question: What will cause the wicked to go away?
records.answer: He will go away at the breath of God’s mouth.

records.question: What reward will the wicked man have for trusting in worthless things?
records.answer: Emptiness will be his reward.

records.question: What will happen to the company of godless people?
records.answer: It will be barren, and fire will consume their tents of bribery.

records.question: What did Job say about the comfort offered by his friends?
records.answer: Job said they were making him more miserable with their endless, useless words.

records.question: How does Job’s speaking affect his grief?
records.answer: If he speaks, his grief is not lessened, and if he keeps from speaking, he is not helped.

records.question: How are other people treating Job as God attacks him?
records.answer: They gape at Job with open mouth, hit him reproachfully on the cheek, and gathered together against him.

records.question: To whom has God given Job?
records.answer: God handed him over to the ungodly and threw him into the hands of wicked people.

records.question: How has God injured Job?
records.answer: He has pierced Job’s kidneys and poured out his bile on the ground.

records.question: What has Job done to his skin to show his grief?
records.answer: He has sewn sackcloth on his skin.

records.question: Who is Job’s witness and able to vouch for Job?
records.answer: Job’s witness is in heaven, and the one who is for him is on high.

records.question: Who does Job turn to as his friends scoff at him?
records.answer: Job pours out his tears to God.

records.question: What must Job always see?
records.answer: He must always see the provocation of the mockers who are with him.

records.question: What pledge does Job want God to make to Job?
records.answer: He wants God to pledge himself to be a guarantee for Job.

records.question: Whose evil deed will cause the eyes of his children to fail?
records.answer: The one who denounces his friends for a reward will cause the eyes of his children to fail.

records.question: What has happened to Job’s eye and his body because of sorrow?
records.answer: His eye is dim and all his body parts are as thin a shadow.

records.question: Does Job think that he can find a wise man among his friends?
records.answer: Job knows that he will not find a wise man among them.

records.question: Does Job have plans for the future?
records.answer: Job’s plans are over, as are the wishes of his heart.

records.question: What has become Job’s father, mother, and sister?
records.answer: The pit has become his father, and the worm is his mother and sister.

records.question: How did Bildad think Job viewed his friends?
records.answer: Bildad thought Job regarded them as beasts and thought they were stupid.

records.question: What will happen to the light of the wicked person?
records.answer: His light goes out; the flame of his fire will not shine.

records.question: What will throw the wicked man into a net?
records.answer: He will be thrown into a net by his own feet, and he will walk into a pitfall.

records.question: What will catch the wicked man?
records.answer: He will be caught by a trap, a snare, and a noose.

records.question: What will happen to the strength of the wicked man?
records.answer: His strength will turn into hunger.

records.question: Where will the wicked man no longer live?
records.answer: He will no longer live in his tent but will be unable to save himself.

records.question: What image does Bildad use to describe what will happen to the wicked man?
records.answer: He describes the wicked man as a tree whose roots will dry up beneath the ground, and whose branch will wither above.

records.question: Will the wicked man have any descendants?
records.answer: He will have no son or son’s son among his people, nor any remaining kinfolk where he had stayed.

records.question: How do the people respond to what happens to the wicked man?
records.answer: People will be shocked and horrified at what happens to the wicked man.

records.question: What does Job ask his friends to stop doing to him?
records.answer: Job asks his friends to stop hurting him and discouraging him.

records.question: How many times have Job’s friends reproached him?
records.answer: They have reproached him ten times.

records.question: Whose concern should it be if Job had erred?
records.answer: Job says the error should be his own concern.

records.question: How does Job say God has treated him?
records.answer: Job says God has done wrong to Job and caught him in God’s net.

records.question: What happens when Job calls out for help because he has been wronged?
records.answer: He is not answered and there is no justice.

records.question: According to Job, how has God regarded Job?
records.answer: Job says God has regarded him as one of his enemies.

records.question: What has happened to all of Job’s family and friends?
records.answer: God has put his brothers far from him, his acquaintances are alienated, his kinsfolk fail him, and his close friends have forgotten him.

records.question: How does Job’s servant respond to Job when he calls him?
records.answer: His servant does not respond when Job gives an order.

records.question: How have Job’s former friends treated him?
records.answer: His former friends have turned against him.

records.question: How does Job survive?
records.answer: He survives only with the skin of his teeth.

records.question: What does Job want to happen to his words?
records.answer: He wants them to be written down and inscribed in a book, or engraved with pen and lead in the rock forever.

records.question: What does Job say he knows?
records.answer: He knows that his Redeemer lives, and that at last his Redeemer will stand on the earth.

records.question: What does Job say will happen when his body is destroyed?
records.answer: Job in his flesh will see God.

records.question: What does wrath bring?
records.answer: Wrath brings the punishment of the sword.

records.question: Why did Zophar answer Job quickly?
records.answer: He answered Job quickly he was troubled by what Job said. He hears Job’s rebuke and says it puts him to shame.

records.question: How long does the joy of a godless man last?
records.answer: The joy of the godless only lasts for a moment.

records.question: How will the wicked man perish?
records.answer: He will perish permanently, like garbage disappears.

records.question: How will the wicked man go away?
records.answer: He will fly away like a dream, and be chased away like a vision of the night.

records.question: What will the wicked man’s children do?
records.answer: His children will apologize to poor people.

records.question: What happens to wickedness inside the wicked man?
records.answer: It will cause the food in his intestines to turn bitter, and will becomes like the poison of asps inside him.

records.question: What will happen to the riches that the wicked man swallows down?
records.answer: He will vomit them up again.

records.question: What will the wicked man not live to enjoy?
records.answer: He will not live to enjoy the blessings that flow from God.

records.question: Why will the wicked man not rejoice?
records.answer: He has oppressed and neglected the poor people, and has violently taken away houses that he did not build.

records.question: Why will the prosperity of the wicked man not be permanent?
records.answer: It will not be permanent because there is nothing left that he did not devour.

records.question: What will God do to the wicked man who is about to fill his belly?
records.answer: God will rain down the fierceness of his wrath on him while he is eating.

records.question: What will happen when the wicked man flees from the iron weapon?
records.answer: A bow of bronze will shoot him.

records.question: What will the heavens and the earth do against the wicked man?
records.answer: The heavens will reveal his iniquity and the earth will be a witness against him.

records.question: What will happen to the wicked man on the day of God’s wrath?
records.answer: The wealth of his house will vanish and his goods will flow away.

records.question: What does Job think his friends will do after he has spoken?
records.answer: He thinks they will continue to mock him.

records.question: How will people respond when they look at Job?
records.answer: They will be astonished and lay their hands upon their mouths.

records.question: What happens to Job when he thinks about his sufferings?
records.answer: He is terrified; his flesh trembles.

records.question: What does Job ask about wicked people?
records.answer: Job asks, “Why do they continue to live, become old, and grow mighty in power?”

records.question: What happens to the bull and the cow of the wicked?
records.answer: The bull does not fail to breed and the cow does not lose her calf prematurely.

records.question: What do the wicked say to God?
records.answer: They tell God to depart from them, for they do not wish any knowledge of his ways.

records.question: How does Job respond to the advice of wicked people?
records.answer: He wants nothing to do with their advice.

records.question: Who does Job want to pay for the guilt of the wicked person?
records.answer: Job wants the wicked person to pay for his guilt, and not his children, so that he would know his guilt.

records.question: Can anyone teach God knowledge?
records.answer: No, for he judges even those who are high.

records.question: What happens to both the man who dies in full strength and the one who dies in bitterness of soul?
records.answer: They both lie down alike in the dust and the worms cover them both.

records.question: What does Job know about his friends’ thoughts and ways?
records.answer: He knows their thoughts and the ways in which they wrong him.

records.question: What have traveling people seen happen to the wicked man?
records.answer: They have seen that the wicked man is kept from the day of calamity, and that he is led away from the day of wrath.

records.question: What will men do for the tomb of the wicked man?
records.answer: Men will keep watch over his tomb.

records.question: With what does Job say Zophar was trying to comfort him?
records.answer: Job says Zophar was trying to comfort him with things that are not true.

records.question: What does Eliphaz ask Job if his righteousness can do for the Almighty?
records.answer: He asks if it brings any pleasure to the Almighty if Job is righteous.

records.question: How does Eliphaz mock Job’s reverence for God?
records.answer: He mockingly says that God would not punish Job if Job had truly been righteous.

records.question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of doing to the naked?
records.answer: He says that Job has stripped the naked of their clothing.

records.question: What does Eliphaz accuse Job of doing to widows?
records.answer: He claims Job has sent widows away empty.

records.question: What does Eliphaz say the darkness has done to Job?
records.answer: He says Job is in darkness so that he does not know what to do.

records.question: What does Eliphaz claim Job says about God not seeing people?
records.answer: Job says, “Thick clouds are a covering to God, so that he does not see people.”

records.question: What happens to the foundations of wicked men?
records.answer: The wicked men’s foundations have washed away, as if by a flooding river.

records.question: How do the righteous act when they see the fate of the wicked?
records.answer: The righteous see their fate and are glad.

records.question: What will happen if Job is at peace with God?
records.answer: If Job is at peace with God, good will come to him.

records.question: What does Eliphaz say will happen if Job returns to the Almighty?
records.answer: If Job returns to the Almighty, he will be built up.

records.question: What will happen when Job takes pleasure in the Almighty?
records.answer: When Job takes pleasure in the Almighty, he will lift up his face to God.

records.question: What does God do for the humble?
records.answer: God saves those who are humble.

records.question: Is Job finished protesting?
records.answer: No. Job said that there is much more he could protest about.

records.question: What would Job do before God if he could find him?
records.answer: He would lay his case in order before God and fill his mouth with arguments.

records.question: Does Job think God would argue against him in the greatness of God’s power if he could stand before him?
records.answer: No, he thinks God would listen to him fairly.

records.question: What does Job say God is doing in the south?
records.answer: Job says in the south, God hides himself so that no one can see what he does there.

records.question: What result does Job expect from God’s testing him?
records.answer: When God has tested Job, he will come out like gold.

records.question: What has Job done with the words of God’s mouth?
records.answer: Job has treasured up in his heart the words of God’s mouth.

records.question: What will God carry out for Job?
records.answer: God will carry out his decrees for Job.

records.question: How does Job feel when he thinks about God?
records.answer: When Job thinks about him, he is afraid of him.

records.question: What covers Job’s face?
records.answer: The thick darkness covers Job’s face.

records.question: What times does Job think are not set by the Almighty?
records.answer: Job asks why times for judging the wicked are not set by the Almighty.

records.question: What do the wicked do to the donkey of the fatherless?
records.answer: They drive away the donkey of the fatherless.

records.question: What do the poor hope the Arabah will provide?
records.answer: They hope the Arabah will provide them food for their children.

records.question: What do the poor lack in the cold?
records.answer: They have no covering in the cold.

records.question: What do the poor embrace for lack of shelter?
records.answer: They embrace a rock for lack of shelter.

records.question: What do the poor do for others even though they go hungry?
records.answer: Even though they go hungry, they carry others’ sheaves of grain.

records.question: What do the poor do for others even though they suffer thirst?
records.answer: They tread the wicked men’s winepresses, but they suffer thirst.

records.question: What is the murderer like in the night?
records.answer: In the night, the murderer is like a thief.

records.question: Why do the wicked shut themselves up in daytime?
records.answer: The wicked do not care for the light.

records.question: With what terrors are the wicked comfortable?
records.answer: They are comfortable with the terrors of the thick darkness.

records.question: Who does Sheol consume?
records.answer: Sheol consumes those who have sinned.

records.question: Who does the wicked one devour?
records.answer: The wicked one devours the barren women who have not born children.

records.question: Who does God drag away?
records.answer: God drags away the mighty by his power.

records.question: What will happen to the mighty in a little while?
records.answer: In only a little while, the mighty will be gone.

records.question: Where does God make order?
records.answer: God makes order in his high places of heaven.

records.question: Of whom does Bildad ask can they be clean and acceptable to God?
records.answer: He asks if one who is born of a woman can be clean and acceptable to God.

records.question: To what does Bildad compare a son of man?
records.answer: He says that a son of man is a grub.

records.question: Whose words does Job say Bildad is speaking?
records.answer: Job says Bildad is not speaking God’s words, but his own.

records.question: What has no covering before God?
records.answer: Sheol itself has no covering against God.

records.question: Where does God bind up the waters?
records.answer: He binds up the waters in his thick clouds.

records.question: What does God spread on the face of the moon?
records.answer: He encloses the face of the moon and spreads his cloud on it.

records.question: What did God calm with his power?
records.answer: He calmed the sea with his power.

records.question: By what did God clear the heavens of storms?
records.answer: By his breath, he cleared the heavens of storms.

records.question: How much of God’s ways are people able to see?
records.answer: People can see only the edges of God’s ways.

records.question: What does Job say God has taken away from him?
records.answer: God has taken away his justice.

records.question: What does Job vow his lips will not speak?
records.answer: Job vows that surely his lips will not speak wickedness or deceit.

records.question: How long will Job’s thoughts not reproach him?
records.answer: His thoughts will not reproach him so long as he lives.

records.question: What does Job say God does when he cuts off a godless man’s life?
records.answer: When God cuts off his life, God will punish him for the wrong things that he has done.

records.question: What does Job say he will not conceal of the Almighty?
records.answer: Job said that he would not conceal the hand of the Almighty.

records.question: Of what will the wicked man’s offspring not have enough?
records.answer: His offspring will never have enough food.

records.question: What will the wicked man’s widow not do for him?
records.answer: His widow will make no lament for him.

records.question: What will happen to the silver of the wicked man?
records.answer: The innocent will divide up his silver among themselves.

records.question: What does the wicked man see when he opens his eyes after he lies down rich?
records.answer: He opens his eyes, and everything is gone.

records.question: What does the east wind do as it carries the wicked man away?
records.answer: The east wind carries him away, and it sweeps him out of his place.

records.question: What does the wicked man try to do when the east wind does not stop?
records.answer: He tries to flee out of its power.

records.question: From where is copper smelted?
records.answer: Copper is smelted out of stone.

records.question: What does man search out to the farthest limit?
records.answer: Man searches out, to the farthest limit, the stones of gloom and thick darkness.

records.question: Where does man break open a shaft?
records.answer: He breaks open a shaft away from where people live.

records.question: What is contained in the dust of the earth?
records.answer: The earth’s dust contains gold.

records.question: What has not walked through the path of man’s shaft?
records.answer: The proud animals have not walked such a path, nor has the fierce lion passed there.

records.question: What does man see in the channels he cuts among the rocks?
records.answer: His eye sees every valuable thing there.

records.question: Where are wisdom and understanding not found?
records.answer: Both of these are not found in the land of the living.

records.question: What cannot equal the worth of wisdom and understanding?
records.answer: Gold and crystal cannot equal both of these in worth.

records.question: The price of wisdom is more than what jewel?
records.answer: The price of wisdom is more than rubies.

records.question: From whose eyes is wisdom hidden?
records.answer: Wisdom is hidden from the eyes of all living things.

records.question: Who knows wisdom’s place?
records.answer: God understands the way to wisdom and he knows its place.

records.question: What did God parcel out by measure?
records.answer: He parceled out the waters by measure.

records.question: For what did God make a decree?
records.answer: He made a decree for the rain.

records.question: What did God tell people is wisdom?
records.answer: To people, God said, “See, the fear of the Lord—that is wisdom.”

records.question: Does Job recall a time when God cared for him?
records.answer: Job remembers that in the past months God had cared for him.

records.question: What was on Job’s tent in the ripeness of his days?
records.answer: Job remembers the ripeness of his days, when the friendship of God was on his tent.

records.question: What had the rock poured out for Job in the past?
records.answer: When the almighty was with Job, the rock poured out for him streams of oil.

records.question: How did the young men show respect for Job in the city square?
records.answer: They saw Job and kept their distance from him in respect.

records.question: What did the princes do in the past when Job came?
records.answer: They used to refrain from talking when he came.

records.question: What happened to the tongue of the noblemen when Job came?
records.answer: Their tongue clung to the roof of their mouths.

records.question: What would the noblemen do after their eyes saw Job?
records.answer: They would then give witness to Job and approve of him.

records.question: What did Job cause the widow’s heart to do?
records.answer: He caused her heart to be glad.

records.question: What had Job done even for the person he did not know?
records.answer: He would examine the case even of one whom he did not know.

records.question: Who would Job pluck from the teeth of the unrighteous?
records.answer: He plucked the victim out from between the teeth of the unrighteous.

records.question: What does Job say is always new in his hand?
records.answer: The bow of his strength is always new in his hand.

records.question: What did men wait to drink in like rain from Job?
records.answer: They opened their mouth wide to drink in his words as they would for the latter rain.

records.question: To what does Job compare himself at a funeral?
records.answer: He say that he is like one who comforts mourners at a funeral.

records.question: Who has nothing but mockery for Job?
records.answer: Those who are younger than Job have nothing but mockery for him.

records.question: What made the young men’s fathers thin?
records.answer: They were thin from poverty and hunger.

records.question: From where were the young men’s fathers driven out?
records.answer: Their fathers were driven out from among people.

records.question: Of whom does Job say the young men’s fathers are descendants?
records.answer: Job says that they were descendants of fools, indeed, of worthless men.

records.question: What had Job become for the sons of the worthless men?
records.answer: Job had become their subject for a song of mockery.

records.question: What do the people now cast away in front of Job?
records.answer: These people cast away self-restraint in front of him.

records.question: Why are the men able to advance his calamity for Job?
records.answer: They advance his calamity because there is no one to hold them back.

records.question: What does Job say is driven away by the wind?
records.answer: His dignity is driven away as if by the wind.

records.question: What has laid hold of Job as his life is pouring out within him?
records.answer: Many days of suffering have laid hold on him.

records.question: What does Job say has changed his clothing?
records.answer: Skin disease has changed his skin, referred to as clothing.

records.question: How does Job say God has changed?
records.answer: God has changed and become cruel to him; with the power of his hand God persecutes him.

records.question: What does Job know is destined for all living things?
records.answer: He knows that God will bring him to death, to the house destined for all living things.

records.question: What came when Job waited for light?
records.answer: When he waited for light, darkness came instead.

records.question: Where did Job stand to call for help?
records.answer: He stood up in the assembly and cried for help.

records.question: For what kind of music does Job say his harp is tuned?
records.answer: Job says that his harp is tuned for songs of mourning.

records.question: What desire does Job say is subdued by a covenant with his eyes?
records.answer: Job has made a covenant with his eyes to not look with desire on a virgin.

records.question: For whom did Job use to think calamity was reserved?
records.answer: Job used to think that calamity was for the unrighteous.

records.question: What does Job ask to be done so that God would know his integrity?
records.answer: He asks to be weighed in an even balance, so that God would know his integrity.

records.question: What does Job ask to happen to the harvest if he has turned out of the right way?
records.answer: He says to let the harvest be uprooted out of his field.

records.question: What does Job say should be the judgement if he was attracted to another woman?
records.answer: Job says to let his wife grind grain for another man.

records.question: What kind of fire does Job say this crime is like?
records.answer: Job says that it is like a fire that consumes everything.

records.question: What did God do for both the servants and for Job?
records.answer: God made and molded them all in the womb.

records.question: How does Job say he has treated the orphan from his youth?
records.answer: He says the orphan grew up with him as with a father.

records.question: What should be offered to warm the needy with no clothing?
records.answer: They should have been warmed with the wool of his sheep.

records.question: What part of his body does Job say should come off if he has failed to have compassion?
records.answer: Job says to let his upper arm fall from the shoulder blade.

records.question: What could people say to fine gold?
records.answer: They could say to fine gold, “You are my confidence.”

records.question: Who would Job be denying if he worshiped the sun or moon?
records.answer: If he worshiped them, he would have denied the God who is above.

records.question: How has Job not suffered his mouth to sin?
records.answer: Job has not suffered his mouth to sin by asking for the life of those who hate him with a curse.

records.question: What had Job always done for the traveler?
records.answer: He had always opened his doors to the traveler.

records.question: How does Job say mankind has hidden his sins?
records.answer: Job says mankind hides sins by hiding his guilt in his chest.

records.question: What does Job want to have that his opponent has written?
records.answer: Job desired to have the indictment that his opponent had written.

records.question: How would Job go up to his opponent if he had their indictment?
records.answer: He would go up to him as a confident prince.

records.question: If Job has caused landowners to lose their lives, what does he call to grow instead of crops?
records.answer: Job said to let thorns grow instead of wheat and weeds instead of barley.

records.question: What did Job’s three friends do when they could not convince Job that he had done anything wrong?
records.answer: They stopped answering Job.

records.question: What emotion was kindled in Elihu when Job continued to justify himself rather than God?
records.answer: Elihu’s anger was kindled against Job.

records.question: Why was Elihu angry with Job’s three friends?
records.answer: Elihu was angry with Job’s friends because they had not been able to answer Job but they had still declared that he was wrong.

records.question: Why was Elihu timid and afraid to tell Job and his friends what he was thinking?
records.answer: Elihu was young and the others were all very old and should be able to teach wisdom.

records.question: Who does Elihu say gives understanding to man?
records.answer: The breath of the Almighty gives man understanding.

records.question: Why does Elihu say the others should listen to him and allow him to declare what he knows?
records.answer: It is not only the great who are wise, and it not the aged alone who understand justice.

records.question: What were Job’s friends not able to do even though Elihu waited for them to speak, and paid attention carefully?
records.answer: Job’s friends were not able to prove Job wrong or respond to his words.

records.question: Who does Elihu say must refute Job when the three friends, who thought they were wise, were not able to do that?
records.answer: It is God who must refute Job.

records.question: What does Elihu decide to do because the three friends were dumbfounded and could not answer Job?
records.answer: Elihu decided that because the friends had not a word more to say, he will not wait any longer.

records.question: What is it that compels Elihu to share his knowledge with Job?
records.answer: The spirit compels Elihu to share his knowledge.

records.question: What does Elihu say he is feeling like within his breast?
records.answer: He says his breast feels like wine in new wineskins that are ready to burst.

records.question: What does Elihu say his Maker would do to him if he were to speak and give honorific titles to any man?
records.answer: Elihu says that his Maker would soon take him away.

records.question: Why does Elihu beg Job to listen to the words he will speak?
records.answer: Elihu begs Job to listen because he will speak from the uprightness of his heart.

records.question: Who has made Elihu and what has given him life?
records.answer: The Spirit of God made Elihu and the Almighty gave him life.

records.question: What does Elihu ask Job to do if Job could answer Elihu?
records.answer: He asks Job to set his words in order and stand up before Elihu.

records.question: What reason does Elihu give that Job should not be afraid of him or feel pressure from Elihu?
records.answer: Elihu tells Job that they are the same in God’s sight and were both formed out of the clay.

records.question: What had Elihu heard Job saying?
records.answer: Elihu heard Job saying that he was clean, without transgression, innocent and there was no sin in him.

records.question: Who does Job blame for finding opportunities to attack him, and for regarding him as an enemy?
records.answer: Job blames God for doing these things.

records.question: How does Elihu say God compares to man?
records.answer: Elihu says God is greater than man.

records.question: Why does Elihu say it is useless to struggle against God?
records.answer: God does not have to account for any of his doings.

records.question: How does Elihu say that God speaks to man?
records.answer: God speaks in a dream and in a vision during the night while men are sleeping.

records.question: Why does God open the ears of men and frighten them with threats?
records.answer: God does this in order to pull man back from sinful purposes and keep pride from him.

records.question: What does Elihu say is the reason that man has pain on his bed, agony in his bones, and no desire for food or delicacies?
records.answer: Elihu says that this is because man is being punished.

records.question: What does Elihu say happens to a man who is being punished by God?
records.answer: A man’s flesh is consumed, his bones stick out and his soul draws close to the pit.

records.question: What could an angel mediator say to God to save a person from going down to the pit?
records.answer: The angel could say to God, “I have found a ransom for him.”

records.question: What will happen to the flesh of the person who is saved from going down to the pit?
records.answer: His flesh will become fresher than a child’s.

records.question: What will happen to the life of a person who admits his sin and is rescued from the pit by God?
records.answer: That person’s life will continue to see light.

records.question: Why does Elihu say that God rescues a person from the pit?
records.answer: God does this so that a person may be enlightened with the light of life.

records.question: What does Elihu want to teach Job if Job will pay attention and listen to him and remain silent?
records.answer: Elihu wants to teach Job wisdom.

records.question: Who does Elihu want to listen to his words and hear him?
records.answer: Elihu wants the wise men and those who have knowledge to listen to him.

records.question: What does Elihu want others to choose and discover for themselves?
records.answer: Elihu wants them to choose what is just and discover what is good.

records.question: What does Job say that God has taken away from him even though he is righteous?
records.answer: Job says that God has taken away his justice.

records.question: In whose company does Elihu say Job goes around?
records.answer: He says Job goes around in the company of those who do evil.

records.question: What does Elihu tell the men of understanding that God does not do?
records.answer: God does not do wickedness, commit sin, or pervert justice.

records.question: What does Elihu say would happen if God ever gathered back to himself his spirit and his breath?
records.answer: All flesh would perish and mankind would return to dust.

records.question: Who does Elihu’s question imply that Job is condemning?
records.answer: He implies Job is condemning God, who is righteous and mighty.

records.question: Who does Elihu say are the works of God’s hands?
records.answer: All people, rich and poor, are the work of God’s hands.

records.question: What does Elihu say that God sees?
records.answer: Elihu says that God sees a person’s ways and all his steps.

records.question: What does God do in the night to mighty men whose ways and deeds he knows?
records.answer: God overthrows them in the night and they are destroyed.

records.question: What will God do to those who do wicked deeds like criminals and make the cry of the poor come to him?
records.answer: God will kill them in the open sight of others.

records.question: Over whom does God rule?
records.answer: God rules over the nation and the individual alike.

records.question: What is Elihu suggesting that Job should admit to God?
records.answer: Elihu suggests that Job should admit that he is guilty and has committed sin, but will do it no longer.

records.question: What will men of understanding say about Job?
records.answer: They will say that Job speaks without knowledge and understanding.

records.question: What does Elihu say Job is adding to his sin because of his talking like wicked men?
records.answer: He says that Job is adding transgression to his sin.

records.question: How does Elihu imply Job compares himself to God?
records.answer: Elihu implies that Job thinks he is innocent, and that he is more righteous than God.

records.question: What does Elihu tell Job and his friends to look up and see?
records.answer: Elihu tells them to look up and see the sky.

records.question: What effect could Job’s wickedness or his righteousness have on another man?
records.answer: Job’s wickedness could hurt a man and his righteousness could benefit another human.

records.question: Why do people cry out for help from the arms of mighty men?
records.answer: They cry out for help because of the many acts of oppression done to them by others who are more powerful than they are.

records.question: What things does Elihu say that God can do for people even though no one acknowledges it?
records.answer: God teaches us and makes us wise.

records.question: Why does Elihu say that God does not give an answer when people cry out to him?
records.answer: Elihu says that God does not give an answer when people cry out but proudly continue in sin.

records.question: What will God certainly not hear?
records.answer: He will certainly not hear prayers that lack sincerity.

records.question: What does Elihu accuse Job of doing when Job opens his mouth?
records.answer: He says Job opens his mouth to speak foolishness and to pile up words without knowledge.

records.question: To whom does Elihu acknowledge that righteousness belongs?
records.answer: Elihu acknowledges that righteousness belongs to his Maker.

records.question: What does God do for those who those who suffer?
records.answer: He does what is right for those who suffer.

records.question: What does God do for the righteous?
records.answer: He sets them on thrones like kings forever, and they are lifted up.

records.question: What does God reveal to those who are bound in chains and trapped in cords of suffering?
records.answer: He reveals to them what they have done, their transgressions, and how they behaved arrogantly.

records.question: What will happen to those who listen to God and worship him?
records.answer: They will spend their days in prosperity and their years in contentment.

records.question: What will happen to the people who do not listen to God?
records.answer: They will perish by the sword and die because they have no knowledge.

records.question: What happens to godless people who keep their anger and do not cry out to God for help?
records.answer: They die in their youth and their lives end in disgrace.

records.question: How does Elihu say God uses affliction and oppression?
records.answer: God uses suffering to keep people from perishing because of their sins.

records.question: What does Elihu say that God would like to do for Job?
records.answer: God would like to draw Job out of his distress and into a place of happiness and prosperity.

records.question: What has filled Job?
records.answer: He is full of the judgment on the wicked.

records.question: What things could lead Job to deception and turn him aside from justice?
records.answer: Anger with God could lead Job to deception, and a great bribe would not buy his pardon.

records.question: What things will not be able to help Job out of his distress?
records.answer: Job’s wealth and the force of his strength will not help him out of his distress.

records.question: Why does Elihu tell Job to be careful?
records.answer: He says Job would rather defy God than learn what God wants to teach him through suffering.

records.question: What can no one say about God?
records.answer: No one can say that God has committed unrighteousness.

records.question: What is it about God that we cannot calculate?
records.answer: We cannot calculate the number of his years.

records.question: How does God cause rain to fall?
records.answer: He draws up the drops of water and puts it in clouds which pour rain down and drop it in abundance on mankind.

records.question: Why does Elihu say that God spreads lightning and covers the sea with darkness?
records.answer: He spreads lightning around himself and covers the sea with darkness in order to judge people and give food in abundance.

records.question: What tells people and cattle of the coming storm?
records.answer: The thunder tells people and cattle of the coming storm.

records.question: What makes Elihu’s heart tremble?
records.answer: The noise of God’s voice and the sound of his roar causes Elihu’s heart to tremble.

records.question: What does God tell the snow and the rain to do?
records.answer: He tells the snow to fall to the earth, and the rain to become a great shower of rain.

records.question: Why does God stop the hand of every man from working?
records.answer: God stops them so that all people may see his deeds.

records.question: For what reason do the beasts go into hiding and stay in their dens?
records.answer: They hide and stay in their dens because of the storms that come.

records.question: What is given by the breath of God?
records.answer: By the breath of God ice is given.

records.question: For what reasons does God give guidance to the clouds and cause them to do whatever he commands?
records.answer: He makes this happen sometimes for correction, sometimes to water his land, and sometimes to provide rain for crops to feed people.

records.question: About what does Elihu want Job to stop and think?
records.answer: He wants Job to stop and think about God’s marvelous deeds.

records.question: What happens when God forces his will on the clouds?
records.answer: God makes lightning bolts flash in the clouds.

records.question: What image does Elihu use to describe the sky?
records.answer: He says the sky is as strong as a mirror of cast metal.

records.question: Why does Elihu say that he and others cannot lay out their arguments before God?
records.answer: They cannot lay out their arguments before God because of the darkness of their minds.

records.question: What is it that people cannot look at when the sky is clear?
records.answer: People cannot look at the sun when it is bright in the sky.

records.question: What does Elihu say that the Almighty does not do to people?
records.answer: The Almighty does not mistreat people, acting unjustly.

records.question: To whom does Elihu say that the Almighty does not pay attention?
records.answer: The Almighty does not pay attention to those who are wise in their own minds.

records.question: Out of what did Yahweh speak to Job?
records.answer: Yahweh spoke to Job out of a fierce storm.

records.question: By what means did someone darken counsel?
records.answer: By speaking without knowledge, Job made it harder for people to understand God’s actions.

records.question: What does Yahweh tell Job he must do when Yahweh questions him?
records.answer: Job must gird up his loins like a man and answer Yahweh’s questions.

records.question: What sang together and who shouted for joy when Yahweh laid the cornerstone of the earth?
records.answer: The morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy when the cornerstone of the earth was laid.

records.question: To what does Yahweh compare the sea bursting out after it was shut up with doors?
records.answer: God compares the sea bursting out of doors to coming out of the womb.

records.question: What did Yahweh put in place to mark out the boundary of the sea so that it could come only so far and no farther?
records.answer: Yahweh put in place bars and doors to mark a boundary for the sea.

records.question: How is the earth changed in appearance like clay changes under a seal?
records.answer: The light of dawn changes the earth so that all things on it stand out clearly, like the folds of a piece of clothing seen in the light.

records.question: What does Yahweh say to mock Job about his lack of knowledge about the way to the resting place of light and darkness?
records.answer: Yahweh mocks Job by saying that undoubtedly Job should know about this because he was born then and the number of his days is so large.

records.question: For what reason does Yahweh say he has kept storehouses for the snow and the hail?
records.answer: Yahweh has kept these storehouses for times of trouble and for a day of battle and war.

records.question: Why does Yahweh cause it to rain on the wilderness in which there is no person?
records.answer: He causes it to rain in order to meet the needs of the barren and lonely regions and to make the tender grass sprout up.

records.question: What does Yahweh ask Job if he can do to Pleiades and Orion?
records.answer: He asks Job if he can tie the bands on the Pleiades or undo the cords of Orion.

records.question: What happens to the dust and clods of earth when Yahweh pours out water on them?
records.answer: The dust runs into a hard mass and the clods of earth clump tightly together.

records.question: Where do the young lion cubs wait for their food?
records.answer: They crouch in their dens and shelter in hiding to lie in wait.

records.question: Why do the young ones of the ravens stagger about?
records.answer: They stagger about for lack of food.

records.question: What happens to the young deer after they grow up in the open fields?
records.answer: They go out and do not come back again.

records.question: What has Yahweh made the house of the wild donkey?
records.answer: Yahweh has made the Arabah the house of the wild donkey.

records.question: Where does the wild donkey find food?
records.answer: He roams over the mountains where he looks for every green plant to eat.

records.question: What does Yahweh ask Job to make the wild ox do with a rope?
records.answer: He asks Job if, with a rope, he can make the wild ox plow the furrows or harrow the valleys for him.

records.question: What does the ostrich flap proudly?
records.answer: The ostrich flaps its wings proudly as it runs fast.

records.question: What does the ostrich do with her eggs?
records.answer: She leaves her eggs on the earth, and lets them keep warm in the dust.

records.question: Why does the ostrich not fear that her labor might have been in vain?
records.answer: Yahweh has deprived her of wisdom and not given her any understanding.

records.question: What does Yahweh say the ostrich does when she runs?
records.answer: She laughs in scorn at the horse and its rider.

records.question: What clothes the neck of the horse?
records.answer: A flowing mane clothes its neck.

records.question: How does the horse react to the sword?
records.answer: He does not turn back from the sword.

records.question: What can the horse not do at the sound of the trumpet?
records.answer: It cannot stand in one place.

records.question: Where does the eagle make his nest and his home?
records.answer: He makes his nest in high places, and his home on the peaks of the crags.

records.question: How did Job do to show that he was too insignificant to answer Yahweh?
records.answer: Job put his hand over his mouth.

records.question: From what did Yahweh answer Job?
records.answer: Yahweh answered Job from out of a fierce storm.

records.question: What did Yahweh tell Job to do to prepare to answer Yahweh?
records.answer: He told Job to gird up his loins like a man.

records.question: Why did Yahweh say that Job was condemning Yahweh?
records.answer: He said Job condemned Yahweh so that Job could claim he was right.

records.question: With what does Yahweh challenge Job to clothe himself?
records.answer: He challenges Job to cloth himself with glory, splendor, greatness and majesty.

records.question: What does Yahweh tell Job to do to the wicked people?
records.answer: Yahweh tells Job to trample them down where they stand.

records.question: What does the Behemoth eat?
records.answer: He eats grass like an ox.

records.question: What is the tail of the Behemoth like?
records.answer: His tail is like a cedar.

records.question: What is one of the strongest animals God made?
records.answer: God says the Behemoth is the first of the ways of God, meaning first in strength.

records.question: Where does the Behemoth lie?
records.answer: He lies under the lotus plants in the shelter of the reeds.

records.question: What does the Behemoth think when the river floods and the Jordan surges?
records.answer: He does not tremble and he is confident.

records.question: With what does Yahweh ask Job if he can draw out Leviathan?
records.answer: Yahweh asks Job if he can draw out Leviathan with a fishhook.

records.question: What does God ask Job might happen if the fishermen were to catch Leviathan?
records.answer: He asks Job if the fishermen would bargain for Leviathan or divide him up to trade among the merchants.

records.question: What will happen if a person puts his hand on Leviathan?
records.answer: It someone puts his hand on the Leviathan just once, he will remember the battle and do it no more.

records.question: Since no one is fierce enough to dare stir Leviathan up, can anyone stand before Yahweh?
records.answer: No one dares to stir Leviathan up, so there is no one who can stand before Yahweh.

records.question: How else does Yahweh describe Leviathan’s mouth?
records.answer: He says it is the doors of his face, ringed with teeth, which are a terror.

records.question: How close are the scales on the back of Leviathan?
records.answer: One is so near to another that no air can come between them.

records.question: How does Yahweh say Leviathan’s eyes are like?
records.answer: His eyes are like eyelids of the dawn, bright and glowing.

records.question: What comes out of Leviathan’s mouth?
records.answer: Out of Leviathan’s mouth go flames and fiery sparks.

records.question: What is the smoke from Leviathan’s nostrils like?
records.answer: It is like a boiling pot on a fire that has been fanned to be very hot.

records.question: What is Leviathan’s heart like?
records.answer: His heart is as hard as a lower millstone.

records.question: What do the mighty do when Leviathan raises himself up?
records.answer: They become afraid and draw back.

records.question: What happens when a sword, spear, arrow or any pointed weapon strikes Leviathan?
records.answer: They do nothing to him.

records.question: What does Leviathan think of iron and bronze?
records.answer: He thinks of iron as if it were straw and bronze as if it were rotten wood.

records.question: What kind of trail does Leviathan leave?
records.answer: He leaves a spreading trail in the mud as if he were a threshing sledge.

records.question: What does he make the deep to do?
records.answer: He makes the deep to foam up like a boiling pot of water.

records.question: Why does Leviathan have no equal on earth?
records.answer: He s has been made to live without fear.

records.question: What did Job acknowledge that he had spoken?
records.answer: He had spoken things that he did not understand, things too difficult for him to understand, which he did not know about.

records.question: How did Job respond to Yahweh after seeing him with his eye?
records.answer: Job despised himself and repented in dust and ashes.

records.question: What did Yahweh say that Eliphaz and his two friends had done wrong?
records.answer: They had not said right things about Yahweh, as Job had done.

records.question: What did Yahweh tell Eliphaz to give as an offering?
records.answer: He told Eliphaz to take seven bulls and seven rams to offer for themselves as a burnt offering.

records.question: Whose prayer did Yahweh say he would accept?
records.answer: Yahweh said he would accept Job’s prayer.

records.question: What happened after Job prayed for his friends?
records.answer: Yahweh restored his fortunes and gave him twice what he had possessed before.

records.question: What did every person give to Job when they came to comfort him?
records.answer: They each gave him a piece of silver and an earring of gold.

records.question: How did Yahweh bless Job at the end of his life?
records.answer: Yahweh blessed Job more than the first part of Job’s life.

records.question: How many more sons and daughters did Yahweh give to Job?
records.answer: He had seven sons and three daughters.

records.question: What was unique about Job’s daughters?
records.answer: There were no woman in the land as beautiful as Job’s daughters, and he gave them an inheritance with their brothers.
